description: Generate Phase 1 (Repository Intelligence) and Phase 2 (File/Folder Analysis) documentation. Phase 1 produces the top-level ground truth: folder tree, variant detection, tech stack (Markdown), entry points (MASTER_PROMPT.md per variant), and system hypothesis. Phase 2 produces per-variant file-by-file accounting of every file in the repository with purpose, key content, and exclusions.
steps: Create docs/01-repository-intelligence.md with: (a) Full folder tree of the repo collapsed at reasonable depth, (b) Monorepo-style variant listing (all 10 variants with file counts and status), (c) Tech stack per variant (all Markdown, runtime target = AI agents), (d) Entry points per variant (MASTER_PROMPT.md, MASTER_INDEX.md, etc.), (e) Build/tooling (N/A for all), (f) System hypothesis paragraph

Create docs/02-file-folder-analysis/ directory with docs/02-file-folder-analysis/02-file-folder-analysis.md containing: For each of the 10 variant folders + root, document every file's purpose in a table (filename, purpose, key content). Group by variant. Explicitly list excluded items (.git) with reason. Account for all 332 files.

Use the Antigravity example at 'Antigravity with Gemini 3.1 Pro high/01-repository-intelligence.md' and '02-file-folder-analysis/' as style reference but produce ORIGINAL content based on reading the actual repo
Follow OUTPUT_RULES: numbered prefixes, tables for enumerable data, engineering-precise tone, no em-dashes
acceptance_criteria: docs/01-repository-intelligence.md exists with folder tree, all 10 variants listed, tech stack, entry points, hypothesis
docs/02-file-folder-analysis/02-file-folder-analysis.md exists accounting for every folder and file in the repo
No file is silently omitted - every file either documented or explicitly excluded with reason
Content is grounded in actual file reading, not invented from names alone
verification: Confirm docs/01-repository-intelligence.md has sections for folder tree, variants, tech stack, entry points, build/tooling, hypothesis
Spot-check that file purposes match actual content (read a sample of referenced files to verify)
